definition: The task of producing a shorter version of a text that captures its most important information.
details: Summarization approaches include extractive methods (selecting existing sentences from the source) and abstractive methods (generating new sentences that paraphrase and condense the source), with modern LLMs primarily excelling at the latter.

explainer.lead: Text summarization produces a shorter version of a text that captures its most important information. It matters because modern LLMs excel at the abstractive form, making condensed versions of long sources practical.

tiers.eli5: It is like telling someone the key points of a long book instead of making them read all of it.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers choose between extractive methods, which select existing sentences, and abstractive methods, which generate new paraphrased sentences. The pitfall with abstractive output is that new sentences can drift from or distort the source, so faithfulness must be checked.
tiers.paperLevel: Formally the task maps a source text to a shorter text preserving its most important information; extractive methods select source sentences, abstractive methods generate new ones. The known limit is that abstractive summaries can paraphrase and condense but may introduce content not supported by the source.

explainer.example: Condensing a multi-page report into a few paraphrased sentences that state its main findings.
